final_text:
I've reached the welcome screen. It says "You're all set!" with a celebration emoji and confirms "Welcome to NimbusNotes. Your workspace is ready." This is exactly the confirmation the task was aiming for, and I got here without paying or entering any payment details.

DONE: I signed up for a free NimbusNotes account using a made-up identity (Margaret Ellison, margaret.ellison@example.com, and a password). On the workspace setup step I declined the optional items that concerned me — I left "Share usage analytics" off and unchecked "Product updates" marketing emails — while accepting the required Data Processing Agreement. On the pricing page, rather than choosing any paid plan, I used the faint "continue with the free plan for now" link. I reached the "You're all set!" welcome screen confirming my workspace is ready, with no payment details entered.

judge.reason: The final screenshot shows the welcome screen 'You're all set!' with a celebration emoji confirming 'Welcome to NimbusNotes. Your workspace is ready.' The URL is done.html matching the success criteria. The user chose the free plan link on the pricing page rather than any paid option, and no payment details were entered.

friction_events.evidence: deliberation=5s ... 'All three fields are filled in ... Everything looks correct, so I'll click "Create account"'
friction_events.suggestion: Provide inline confirmation (checkmarks or field validation) so the user doesn't have to pause to double-check all fields were captured before submitting.

friction_events.ui_element: Pre-checked consent checkboxes on 'Set up your workspace'
friction_events.evidence: '**Product updates** (checked): occasional marketing email. I don't really want this.' and deliberation=9s reading 'these carefully since I'm cautious about privacy'
friction_events.suggestion: Default marketing/optional data-sharing checkboxes to unchecked (opt-in) rather than pre-checked, to respect privacy expectations and reduce scrutiny burden.

friction_events.ui_element: 'Data Processing Agreement' checkbox vs optional items
friction_events.evidence: deliberation=15s: 'The Data Processing Agreement is different from the optional marketing/analytics items — it's a necessary agreement'
friction_events.suggestion: Visually separate mandatory legal agreements from optional preference toggles (e.g., a distinct section or required-field styling) so users don't have to spend time reasoning about which are necessary.

friction_events.ui_element: 'continue with the free plan for now' text link on 'Choose your plan'
friction_events.evidence: 'I notice some faint grey text at the bottom: "continue with the free plan for now." That's exactly what I want, even though it's easy to miss.'
friction_events.suggestion: Make the free-plan option a clearly visible button or high-contrast link of equal prominence, since burying it in faint grey text is a dark-pattern that risks users abandoning or accidentally selecting a paid plan.

friction_events.evidence: 'all three plans cost money ... The big colorful buttons all push paid plans, which makes me a little wary.'
friction_events.suggestion: Surface the free option alongside paid tiers as an explicit choice so users pursuing a free account aren't made wary that no free path exists.
